o.text: Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kïs- (“short, narrrow, to squize”). Cognate with Karakhanid قِسْغا (qïsɣā), Turkish kısa, Turkmen gysga, Salar qısga, Crimean Tatar qısqa, etc.
Internationalism. From Russian э́тика (étika), ultimately from Ancient Greek ἠθική (ēthikḗ).
Borrowed from Persian قلیان (qalyân), from Arabic غَلْيُون (ḡalyūn), from Italian galeone. Compare Ottoman Turkish قالیون (kalyon), also of Italic origin.
From Old Turkic [script needed] (bilezük, bilerzük, bilersük), composed of bilək (“wrist”) + üzük (“ring”).
